newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand sees more foreign investment in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Thailand sees more foreign investment in 1997.

text.p: Thailand will attract more foreign direct investment in 1997 in line with an expected recovery of its economy, the Board of Investment (BoI) said on Wednesday.
"The expected rise (in foreign investment) next year is based on projected economic growth of seven percent," BoI secretary general Staporn Kavitanond told a news conference.

The government-run board granted tax and other investment incentives to 960 projects worth 535 billion baht ($21.4 billion) in the first 11 months of 1996 against 1,119 projects and 583 billion baht in the same period a year ago, he said.
"Most approved projects are foreign direct investments in vehicle, electronics and chemical industries," Staporn said.

Major investment projects during January/November included General Motors Corp 's car assembly plant, Texas Instruments 's semiconductor plant, and International Business Machines Corp 's hard disk drive plant, he said.
Most approved projects this year are planned Japanese investments, he said.
